newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.78 pct in Dec 8-Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.78 pct in Dec 8-Jan 7.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe), reached 0.78 percent in the Dec 8-Jan 7 period, up from 0.17 percent in the prior four-week period, a Fipe oficial said.
"We are now thinking about January inflation of about one percent," said Juarez Rizzieri, the president of Fipe.
The rise in the index, which measures inflation in the Sao Paulo area, was due mostly to hikes in fuel prices and school matriculation fees, as well as a slowdown in the decline in food prices.
Fipe reported inflation of 0.17 percent in December and 10.03 percent in 1996, its lowest rate since the 1950s.
A hike in fuel prices last month was behind a surge in transportation prices, while education, health care and personal expenses also rose, Rizzieri said.
Fipe is now projecting January inflation of about one percent, he said.
Rizzieri released the following breakdown of the weighted Fipe index for the four-week period ended January 7:
-Personal expenses: 0.96 pct rise in the period
-Health care: 1.79 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
